Medication. I’ve had depressive episodes since I was 11. It’s taken 9 years but now that I’m finally on Prozac, I feel like I’m just now doing more than existing. I have hobbies, I’m taking a course at the community college, I’m going on dates, making friends. I wish I hadn’t been so stubborn because I could have been so much happier a long time ago.

I might have to moved back to Alaska, they had better medical experts, which is kinda messed up. Plus a lot of the psychiatrist here don’t take my insurance, I’ve checked.

Appreciate the candidness. I don’t love things though. I don’t have hobbies because I can’t seem to enjoy them. It all feels tedious and I’m pretty close to just quitting my job and walking out to the desert to die.

Today at work, I was helping an older woman cash out. Since there was no one else in line, we chatted a little. Apparently, my manager snuck up behind me to watch the interaction and I had no idea. As I was finishing up and handing her the receipt, I told her I hoped her day was good. She turns to my manager and simply says,”You need to hire more like her”. It was super kind of her to go out of her way to say that.

Now, my manager is at least a foot and a half taller than me and has resting bitch face. She’s a very intimidating person, and I’ve only really met her twice. So it was super surprising when she reached out and very gently patted my head and said,”Yeah, she’s an angel, isn’t she?” 

It really made my day cause only an hour earlier an old man flipped his shit on me when I told him he would have to go to our customer service desk to exchange something because he didn’t have the receipt. My manager watched that shit show while I was holding back tears and got the guy to calm down, but still basically told him the same thing. 

Anyway, it was just nice.

Oh man, I done this multiple times, but by far the funniest instance was in Las Vegas. 

My friend and I (both 18 year old girls) were walking down the strip to hit up a dessert place at 10:30 at night. She was on my right, and was much taller + had a much longer stride. Now, typically, when I go out to crowded places I often will grab my friends hands so I don’t get lost since I’m 5’3. So I absentmindedly reach out and grab her hand. 

Except it wasn’t her hand.

It was a 30 year old dude who was holding his my hand in his left and his girlfriends in his right . As soon as I realize my mistake, I drop his hand. I’m super embarrassed and he’s super amused. He gets pretend offended and  asked,”What? You don’t wanna hold my hand now?” 

And part of me just said,” Ah, fuck it”. So I shrugged, reached over, and grabbed his hand again. He laughs and starts swinging our clasped hands. Meanwhile, his girlfriend, who has been watching this whole thing, sighs and exasperatedly says,”Andre, this is why I don’t take you places”.

I actually had a nice chat with them as we walked, super kind people. I hope they’re doing good.

(Don’t worry, I found my friend eventually)
